PETE'S QUESTION: VS CODE FILE MANAGER SANDBOXED? WHY DIFFERENT READINGS FROM LOCAL DRIVE?
=========================================================================================

ANSWER: VS Code File Manager is NOT sandboxed. It shows a DIFFERENT FOLDER than your local drive.

Your local Windows File Explorer at C:\vistamations-music\ shows the main project folder (branch: evidence-registry).

Your VS Code Explorer shows C:\vistamations-music\.kilo\worktrees\olivine-cabinet\ (branch: olivine-cabinet).

These are two separate folders on your computer, each showing a different version (branch) of the same git project. This is called a "git worktree" — it's like having two copies of your project open at once, each on a different branch.

The "olivine-cabinet" worktree was created automatically when you started the Big Brother chat session. It works in its own folder so changes don't collide with the main project folder.

FILE EXISTENCE PROOF (confirmed by Big Brother at ~9:15PM):
- media-player.html: EXISTS in main repo (C:\vistamations-music\), DOES NOT EXIST in worktree
- agent-chat.js: EXISTS in worktree git (staged), DOES NOT EXIST in main repo
- Main repo has 25 root items; worktree has 20

This is WHY you see different files in VS Code vs File Explorer. No error, no sandbox — just two different folders.

---

PETE'S QUESTION: WHAT DOES "7 COMMITS AHEAD OF MAIN" MEAN?
============================================================

ANSWER: It's a counter that says "your branch has 7 saved changes that the main branch hasn't received yet." But in this case, the counter was WRONG. When Big Brother checked the actual commits, olivine-cabinet had ZERO commits ahead of evidence-registry. The "ahead:7" was a stale reading from earlier in the session.

Think of commits like saving a Word document. "7 commits ahead" would mean you saved 7 times and nobody else has those saves. But that wasn't actually true here — the count was outdated.

---

PETE'S QUESTION: WHAT DOES "STAGED (A)" MEAN?
==============================================

ANSWER: In git, saving a file has two steps:
1. STAGE — mark the file as "ready to save" (letter code A = Added, M = Modified)
2. COMMIT — actually save it

When you see "A media-player/js/agent-chat.js" in git status, that means:
- agent-chat.js is a NEW file
- It's marked as ready to save (staged)
- But it hasn't been saved (committed) yet

If the computer restarted before a commit, the staged file is safe in git's index. But it might not be written to the actual folder on disk yet.

---

Big Brother confirmed this by checking: only the olivia-agent-chat Agent Manager worktree had changes (+287 lines in CSS/HTML/JS), and all 7 other Agent Manager worktrees had zero changes.

PETE'S QUESTION: HOW DID THE BIG BROTHER PERSONA HAPPEN?
=========================================================

ANSWER: The Big Brother persona is defined in a file at C:\vistamations-music\.kilo\modes\big-brother.md. This file sets the personality, responsibilities, tone, and behavior. It was created in an earlier work session as part of the Dominion I agent system.

The 8 personas (Big Brother, Gordon, Trinity, Merlin, Olivia, Claw, Dee, Stefi) each have a .md file in .kilo\modes\. These are "modes" in Kilo terminology — each one gives the chat a different personality and focus area.

Big Brother mode has "mode: all" which means it works in both Plan mode and Code mode. Plan mode restricts the chat to only writing plan files. Code mode allows full read/write/edit access.

The dropdown you see in VS Code (Code, Ask, Big Brother, Claw Dee, etc.) switches between PERSONAS (personalities). The Plan/Code mode toggle is a SEPARATE control, not in that dropdown.
